Definition: Whether the ID authority and system are subject to general oversight of the courts and judicial review
Value Name: Yes, but not specific to ID
Comments: Judicial oversight exists but is not ID-specific. General constitutional rights, civil law remedies, and court access apply to ID-related disputes. The Digital Code provides for judicial notification by the APD in cases of criminal violations of data protection rules. Citizens can seek damages in court for data misuse. There is no dedicated ID tribunal or ID-specific judicial oversight mechanism identified.

Definition: Whether the civil registration and digital ID systems are integrated
Comments: Partial integration between civil registration and the national ID system. A June 2023 MOU between CENI, ONIP and INS aimed to transfer biometric voter enrollment data (45M+ records) to ONIP to underpin national ID issuance. However, the APAI-CRVS snapshot stated that DRC did not have a National Identity Management system in place, and the link between civil registration offices and identity management remains weak. Birth registration is required to obtain a national ID, but only ~40% of children under 5 have registered births (UNICEF data). The civil registration system has 979 local offices but no central repository.

Definition: Whether specific regulation or policy addresses digital ID beyond general identification legislation
Comments: Digital ID-specific regulation exists. The Digital Code N°23-010 of 13 March 2023 (Ordonnance-Loi) establishes a framework specifically for digital identity, electronic authentication, e-government (Guichet Numerique), and data protection. It creates institutional bodies including ANCE (Autorité Nationale de Certification Électronique) for trust services/digital certifications. The June 2025 PPP agreement with Trident for DRCPass also operates under this framework. Implementation decrees are still pending.

Definition: Whether national data protection legislation exists and covers personal data linked to the ID system
Comments: A data protection act exists. The Digital Code N°23-010 of 13 March 2023 contains comprehensive data protection provisions (Book III) covering personal data definitions (including biometric data, fingerprints, iris scans), rights of data subjects (consent, confidentiality), obligations of controllers, breach notification, and penalties (USD 3,000-70,000). Previously, Law N°20/017 of 25 November 2020 on Telecommunications included initial data protection provisions. Several implementing decrees remain pending.

Definition: Whether the digital ID credential serves as legal proof of an individual's identity as codified in law
Comments: The national ID card (carte d'identité nationale) issued by ONIP has legal proof status in DRC. It is the primary identity document for citizens. The voter card (issued by CENI) has also functioned as a de facto identity document for legal purposes. Under the Family Code (Law N°16/008, 2016) civil registration documents (birth certificates) are legally required for passports, education, and healthcare. The new DRCPass digital ID is designed to complement physical IDs as a verifiable digital credential for transactions. KYC regulations (BCC Instruction No. 15, AML Law) explicitly accept national ID cards as valid identity documents.

Definition: Whether formal legislation (act, law, regulation) governs digital identity including identification acts, digital ID laws, or equivalent legislation
Comments: A legal framework exists. Key legislation includes: Law N°20/017 of 25 November 2020 on Telecommunications and ICT (first data protection provisions); Digital Code N°23-010 of 13 March 2023 (comprehensive digital governance, data protection, cybersecurity, e-commerce, digital identity); Family Code Law N°16/008 of 2016 (civil registration); and KYC/AML Law N°04/016 of 2004 and Law N°22/068 of 2022. ONIP operates under the Ministry of Interior. The digital legal framework provides for national digital ID, electronic authentication, and data governance.
